chapter: Guitar, recordings and Johnny St. Cyr
title: Guitars, strings of lessons and picking style
summary: He used Gibson guitars, no electric at first; his father taught him the MacNeil method; he always used the pick.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, we might go out and talk a little bit more about your guitar now.
Did you start on just an ordinary guitar or did you have an electric? Did you have many electric ones in those days?
No, I didn't have electric guitars.
When did you start on, get that? What kind of an instrument is it? What make?
I have a Gibson guitar. In fact, I've been using Gibson practically all my life.

Supposed to be a good make, I guess you like it then. I was going to ask more about the lessons with your father. Did he teach you with adjusted chart or did you get a guitar book with him pretty soon or what?
Well, he taught me for, he taught a lot of books and sheet music at times and different other little instrumental solos. Yeah. You know, like that.
Well, the MacNeil method was the method I taught him. He was MacNeil method. MacNeil method.
I brought him clean through the MacNeil method. Who publishes that?
Do you remember? I don't, I'm not familiar with those guitar methods. Did you ever... Who publishes that book? Charles MacNeil.
I didn't know if it was somebody like Carl Fisher or somebody like that.
No, I have a Carl Fisher's book, alright, but it's nothing.

I'm going to ask you if you ever did any picking with your fingers, you know, like the classical guitar, the Spanish guitar players like Segovia and all, where they'll pick, you know, where they'll pick with all of their, about three fingers and their thumb, or if you just always used the pick to strum it, what style of guitar?

Well, I did, but I wasn't too successful with it. I think I waited a little too late for that. So you've always used the pick? I've always used the pick. The pick style. I would like to study it, but if I had, you know, time to put it into it. Maybe I could, you know, do a little stuff. Did you, uh, like the guitar.
